morningSnapshot.headline: Global AI Stock Sell-Off Slams Markets as Canadian Unemployment Ticks Up to 6.7%
morningSnapshot.summary: Ryan, global markets are sliding amid a massive tech sell-off, while Statistics Canada reports October's unemployment rate climbing to 6.7% as more job seekers enter the market. Locally in Southern Ontario, federal officials highlight housing investments, and market access agreements offer trade stability.

topStory.headline: Investors dive into bonds as global AI tech selloff continues
topStory.summary: Investors fled to the safety of bonds on Friday as stocks extended their slide in both Europe and Asia after worries around AI wiped trillions of dollars off stock markets.
topStory.whyItMatters: As a long-term investor with a 5-year variable mortgage, major equity corrections driven by tech and AI infrastructure sell-offs ripple across broader market valuations, potentially shifting monetary policy trajectories and bond yields.
topStory.explainMore:
Another wipeout for stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centers is overwhelming Wall Street and global exchanges, erasing previous market gains. Investors rapidly shifted capital into safe-haven bonds as broader market jitters intensified.

Simultaneously, Statistics Canada reported that the national unemployment rate ticked up 0.2 percentage points to 6.7 per cent in October as more individuals, particularly younger Canadians, actively searched for work. This combination of cooling equity markets and a rising unemployment rate provides key context on broader economic momentum following the Bank of Canada's recent rate adjustments.

stories.headline: Chinese state-owned XCMG official facing criminal charges in alleged fraud case
stories.summary: Police in Ontario have filed criminal charges against one of XCMG's officials for allegedly tampering with serial number plates on equipment they were selling in Canada.
stories.whyItMatters: Highlights domestic regulatory enforcement regarding industrial machinery imports and equipment standards within Ontario's industrial sectors.
stories.explainMore: Ontario police action against an official from state-owned XCMG underscores heightened regulatory scrutiny on industrial equipment imports. The charges involve allegations of tampering with serial number plates on heavy machinery marketed in Canada, touching on equipment integrity and trade compliance.

stories.headline: Budget 2026 proposes 1st deposit insurance limit increase in 2 decades
stories.summary: The CDIC limit is moving from $100,000 to $250,000 under the federal budget, an increase many have urged for years to protect consumers.
stories.whyItMatters: Provides expanded federal deposit protection for personal savings and cash holdings for Canadian homeowners and long-term investors.
stories.explainMore: Under the newly proposed federal budget, the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) protection limit will increase significantly from $100,000 to $250,000. This marks the first deposit insurance limit increase in two decades, offering stronger safeguards for cash deposits and consumer savings.

markets.insight: North American markets faced a severe correction today, led by a 4.41% drop in the S&P 500 and a 2.15% decline in the TSX amid the ongoing global tech sell-off. Meanwhile, oil rose 1.93% to $148.21, and the Canadian dollar held at 0.7085 USD.

yourMoney.headline: CDIC Deposit Insurance Limit Set to Rise to $250,000 in Budget 2026
yourMoney.summary: The federal government is moving to increase deposit insurance protection for the first time in 20 years, raising the CDIC limit to $250,000.
yourMoney.whyItMatters: As a homeowner and long-term investor managing cash allocations alongside your 5-year variable mortgage, higher deposit insurance limits provide enhanced security for liquid capital held in CDIC-member institutions.

manufacturing.headline: Minister Sidhu Announces Extension of Favourable Market Access for Key Exports Through 2028
manufacturing.summary: Canada and China have agreed to a two-year extension until the end of 2028 for favourable market access under the Preliminary Joint Arrangement for key Canadian commodities.
manufacturing.whyItMatters: Maintains predictable international trade conditions and export channels, supporting broader Canadian manufacturing and resource supply chains.
manufacturing.engineeringHeadline: Canadian Space Agency Astronaut Prepares for Second Spacewalk
manufacturing.engineeringSummary: Canadian Space Agency astronaut Colonel Joshua Kutryk prepares to conduct his second spacewalk, with livestreams hosted at the John H. Chapman Space Centre, highlighting advanced aerospace engineering and robotics capabilities.

world.headline: Global Stock Markets Reel as AI Tech Sell-Off Erases Midterm Gains
world.summary: A broad liquidation of artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure stocks swept across Wall Street, European, and Asian markets, overriding recent political and midterm market bounces.
world.whyItMatters: Global equity volatility directly influences macroeconomic stability, capital expenditure cycles in high-tech manufacturing, and investor sentiment across international markets.
